description: Lentil (masur) is a cool-season rabi pulse grown mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, often on residual moisture after rice. It fixes its own nitrogen and needs only a small starter dose with phosphorus and sulphur.
npk_split: Apply all N, P and K as basal at sowing along with 20 kg sulphur/ha, and treat the seed with Rhizobium culture.

Ascochyta blight.name: Ascochyta Blight
Ascochyta blight.description: A seed- and residue-borne fungal blight that attacks leaves, stems and pods in cool, wet weather. It causes leaf drop, shoot dieback and shrivelled, discoloured seed.
symptoms: Tan to light brown spots with a darker brown margin on leaflets, stems and pods
Tiny black dots in the centre of the spots
Leaflets drop and shoot tips die back
Ascochyta blight.spread: Comes with infected seed and crop residue and spreads by rain splash during cool, wet spells.
Ascochyta blight.action: Spray chlorothalonil 75 WP 2 g/L or mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L at the first spots and repeat after 10-15 days if wet weather continues.

treatment.name: Chlorothalonil 75 WP
treatment.notes: Protective; most useful at flowering and early pod stage to protect the seed; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP seed treatment
treatment.notes: Use seed from a disease-free crop and treat before sowing; rotate with cereals for 2-3 years.

Powdery mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Powdery mildew.cause: Erysiphe trifolii (often reported in India as Erysiphe polygoni)
Powdery mildew.description: A fungal disease that covers the plant with white powder, usually late in the season on late-sown crops. Severe attack dries the leaves early and gives small, shrivelled seed.
symptoms: White powdery patches on leaflets, stems and pods
Whole plant looks dusted with flour
Leaves turn yellow, curl, dry and drop
Powdery mildew.spread: Airborne spores spread quickly in dry weather with warm days and cool nights.
Powdery mildew.action: Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP 3 g/L at the first white patches and repeat after 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Wettable sulphur 80 WP
treatment.notes: Cover both leaf surfaces; do not spray in very hot afternoon sun.

treatment.name: Timely sowing
treatment.notes: Sow at the recommended time; late-sown lentil is hit hardest.

Rust.name: Rust
Rust.description: The most damaging foliar disease of lentil in north and central India, appearing from flowering in cool, humid weather. Badly affected patches dry up early and look scorched.
symptoms: Yellowish-white pustules on leaflets and pods early in the attack
Brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces, stems and pods
Pustules turn dark brown to black later
Plants dry up early in patches that look burnt
Rust.spread: Wind-borne spores from crop debris and self-sown plants spread in cool, cloudy, humid weather.
Rust.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L or propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/L at the first pustules and repeat after 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Two sprays at 10-12 day intervals from first appearance.

treatment.name: Propiconazole 25 EC
treatment.notes: Use when rust is already spreading in the field; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Rust-resistant varieties
treatment.notes: Grow resistant varieties such as DPL 62 or L 4076 in rust-prone areas and sow early.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The plant shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Keep up regular field scouting.
symptoms: No spots, pustules or powdery growth
healthy.action: Continue weekly scouting, especially from flowering to pod filling.
